cases.formula: =AI("Generate slogan for event in 10 words or less", A2)
cases.description: Existence probe only: AI returns generated text from a model, so no value can be asserted; this records what each engine does with a well-formed call
cases.expected_note: NOT ASSERTABLE BY DESIGN, and deliberately recorded as a probe (expected: null) rather than a support claim -- the treatment batch B gave the CUBE* family and COPILOT, batch C gave DETECTLANGUAGE, and batch G gave RTD, STOCKHISTORY and TRANSLATE. Google's page publishes the syntax `AI("prompt",[optional range])` and the example `=AI("Generate slogan for event in 10 words or less", A2)`, which is the formula this case runs verbatim. THE VALUE IS GENERATED TEXT, NOT A COMPUTED FUNCTION OF THE ARGUMENTS. Google gates the feature -- "This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan." -- and rations it -- "The AI function has short term and long term generation limits." -- and the page's own capability list includes "Access real-time information from Google Search", so an answer may depend on the live web at the moment of evaluation. WHAT GOOGLE DOES NOT SAY, SAID PLAINLY: this page carries no sentence promising that the output varies between runs, so no determinism disclaimer is attributed to Google here. The unassertability is INFERRED from the generative framing and the real-time-search capability quoted above, and is labelled as inference rather than dressed up as documentation. LIBREOFFICE, MEASURED BEFORE THIS FILE WAS AUTHORED. All four pinned builds (24.2.0.3, 24.8.7.2, 25.2.0.3, 25.8.7.3) were probed with NINE storage spellings -- plain, _xlfn., COM.MICROSOFT., ORG.OPENOFFICE., _xlfn.ORG.OPENOFFICE., ORG.LIBREOFFICE., _xlfn.ORG.LIBREOFFICE., _xlfn.COM.MICROSOFT. and COM.SUN.STAR.SHEET.ADDIN.ANALYSIS. -- and every one of those 36 combinations returned #NAME?. LibreOffice's own parser additionally wrote the name back into the converted file LOWER-CASED ('=ai("Say hello")'), which is what it does with an identifier it does not recognise as a function at all rather than with a function it knows under a different storage token. A #NAME? under all nine storage forms on all four builds is therefore a genuine absence and not a storage-form artifact of this harness, which is why 'unsupported in LibreOffice' IS a verdict this file publishes even though the returned VALUE is not assertable in any engine.
